To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) reduction on glucose consumption rates leads to higher GFP production, 2) phenotypic heterogeneities are not necessarily detrimental for bioprocess performance, 3) the highest GFP production is observed in the most heterogeneous system, and 4) the most homogeneous system is the one displaying the lowest GFP production.

growth-dependent recombinant protein production can be improved by engineering of glucose transport, which is prone to phenotypical heterogeneity, and that this heterogeneity may not always be unwanted in bioprocessing applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach for engineering recombinant production strains, based on the control of glucose consumption and on the reduction of acetate production, which is prone to induce population heterogeneity.

the engineering of glucose uptake, which is a fundamental process for the design of recombinant strains, and it has shown that the reduction of glucose uptake rate leads to a significant improvement of GFP production.

the development of a rational strategy for the design of recombinant E. coli strains with high productivity and low phenotypic heterogeneities, by combining genetic engineering with the knowledge of the physiology of glucose metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, depending on the specific bioprocess application, phenotypic heterogenity can be a desirable feature.
the best performance in terms of recombinant product production is obtained when the system is heterogeneous and the rate of glucose consumption is reduced.
, depending on the specific application, heterogeneous and homogeneous populations can be equally advantageous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, when the system under study is bistable, the best performance is achieved by the most heterogeneous populations, which is the case of the strain WGM/pV2.
the engineering of glucose uptake is a promising way for increasing product titer, and that phenotypic segregation is a natural way to achieve it.
, in this particular case, the highest production performance is obtained by combining the highest phenotypic heterogeneities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the engineering of glucose transport can be a useful tool for improving recombinant product yields in microbial systems.
, in order to improve the production performance of a given strain, one should consider not just the average performance, but also the heterogeneity of the population.
, in order to improve the productivity of a recombinant strain, it might be beneficial to increase phenotypic heterogenity, as it has been shown here.
